To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel TP53 14-1 microin-del was identified in a HCC patient with HCV infection; the microindel was associated with impaired p53 signaling and HCV positivity.
a rare TP53 microdeletion was identified in an HCC case with chronic HCV infection, and that HCV-positive HCC cases were significantly associated with TP53 mutations.
we identified a novel type of TP53 mutation, a microindel, in a case of hepatitis C virus ( HCV)-positive hepatocellular carcinoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the correlation of TP53 microindels with HCV infection in HCC, which may be helpful in elucidating the molecular mechanisms underlying hepatocarcinogeneses with HCV infection.
the molecular mechanisms of HCC with chronic HCV infection
the molecular mechanisms of hepatocarcinogensis, which may be useful for the early diagnosis and treatment of HCC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HCCs with HCV infection typically associate with TP53 mutational inactivation, and that TP53 microindels are important contributors to HCC.
HCV is a risk factor for TP53 mutations in HCC.
HCV infection is a risk factor for hepatocarcinoma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HCV infection is associated with TP53 mutations in HCC.
TP53 microindels are important contributors to the development of hepatocarcinomas in HCV-infected patients.
the 14-1 microdeletion of TP53 gene may be a novel mechanism of HCC tumorigenesis in HCV infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TP53 mutations are associated with HCV-positive HCC, but not HBV-positive HCC.

HCV infection may contribute to the development of hepatocellular carcinomas by inducing TP53 microindels, and this is the first report to demonstrate a correlation of HCV positivity and TP53 mutations in hepatocarciongenesis.
TP53 mutations are more frequently observed in HCCs with HCV infections than in those with HBV or without viral infections.
